# Non-Occupational:

# Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) for Exposure to Blood or Body Fluids

# Treatment recommendations:

All persons offered nPEP should be prescribed a 28-day course of a 3-drug antiretroviral regimen.

* IMPORTANT- First dose should be given as soon as possible after exposure
* These medications may be taken with or without food
* Side effects of these medications are infrequent but may include:

nausea, vomiting, diarrha, rash, fever, headaches, insomnia, arthralgias, fatigue, abdominal pain, hepatitis, renal dysfunction, rare lactic acidosis

# Select appropriate treatment below based on renal function:
Creatinine clearance >/= 30 ml/min:
Emtricitabine 200MG/Tenofov AF 25MG Tab 1 PO qday ($$) [R,DI] < AND > Dolutegravir 50MG Tab 1 po qday ($$) [DI] for 28 days
CBOC or after-hours Urgent Care med setups for above
Creatinine clearance < 30 ml/min not on dialysis*:

Emtricitabine 200MG/Tenofovir 300MG Tab 1 po q3days R,DI < AND >

Dolutegravir 50MG Tab 1 po qday [DI] for 28 days

*Optimal dosing is uncertain. Follow-up with ID in 1-2 weeks is recommended to individualize dosing if needed.

# ESRD dialysis:

Emtricitabine 200MG/Tenofov AF 25MG Tab 1 PO qday ($$) [R,DI] < AND > Dolutegravir 50MG Tab 1 po qday ($$) [DI] for 28 days
CBOC or after-hours Urgent Care med setups for the above Note: Dolutegravir is now a recommended agent to be used for HIV treatment and prevention in pregnancy (updated 2023).
